title: vs.audio-bank
description: One SOUND/WAVEnnnn.DAT instrument bank: what playback needs from each instrument record, beside the decoded samples (N.wav and N.sfz per available instrument) in the same directory (Docs/ASSET_PIPELINE.md §6.5, Content/AudioBankJson.hpp). The native loader also checks what a schema cannot: that the directory is audio/banks/<bank_id> and that the instruments fit from first_instrument to slot 255.

display_name.description: Optional informational name, not an identity or gameplay field.

bank_id.description: The bank's id from its disc header. It names this directory, and the sound driver loads the bank by it.

first_instrument.description: Provenance: the instrument slot the disc header names. Playback reads the disc header, so changing this changes nothing; see source_destination for when the driver uses it.

source_destination.description: Provenance: the disc header's sample memory request. 217344 (0x35100) asks for a music area (instrument slot 64 at 0x35100, or 96 at 0x55100), 45312 (0xB100) for a sound effect area (slot 128, 160 or 192); any other value is the address itself, with first_instrument as the slot. Playback reads the disc header, not this.

instruments.description: One per instrument record, in slot order from first_instrument. Playback refuses a bank whose count differs from its disc header's.

curve.description: How the level changes: in equal steps, or by the SPU's exponential curve.

mode.description: A libspu ADSR mode (libspu.h SPU_VOICE_DIRECT to SPU_VOICE_EXPDec).

display_name.description: Optional informational name, not an identity or gameplay field.

available.description: Whether the instrument has a playable sample, and so an N.wav and N.sfz; false for an unused record.

root_note.description: The note, counting 12 per octave, that plays the sample at its recorded 44,100 Hz rate.

fine_tune.description: A pitch scale on every note: a positive value plays it (1 + fine_tune / 32768) times as fast, a negative one (1 + fine_tune / 65536) times, so -32768 is exactly an octave down.

sample_offset.description: Where the sample starts, in bytes into the bank's ADPCM data (16-byte blocks of 28 samples each). Playback adds where the bank lands in sample memory.

loop_offset.description: Where a repeating sample loops back to, in bytes into the same data, unless one of its blocks marks its own loop start; N.sfz holds the decoded loop.

akao3_articulation.description: Provenance, only for an AKAO 3.0 record (bank 32's 64-byte form): what it held beyond the members above. root_note and fine_tune were read from the first pitch and the envelope from the modes and rates; playback reads those members, not this.

pitch_table.description: One pitch per semitone of an octave, where 1048576 plays the sample at its recorded rate.

envelope.description: The SPU ADSR envelope of each note: attack from silence to full level, decay to the sustain level, sustain while the key is held, then release to silence. Rates count 0 as fastest. A sequence's envelope commands can replace parts of it per channel.

attack_rate.description: Each 4 more doubles the attack time; 127 holds the level.

decay_rate.description: Each 1 more doubles the decay time. Decay is always exponential and decreasing.

sustain_level.description: Decay stops at (sustain_level + 1) / 16 of full level.

sustain_direction.description: Whether the level rises or falls while the key is held.

sustain_rate.description: Each 4 more doubles the sustain time; 127 holds the level until the key is released.

release_rate.description: Each 1 more doubles the release time; 31 holds the level. Release always decreases.
